### svc-nixl · 2026-09-18

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-non-gpu` · commit `08ab175b`

**TL;DR:** The `Test Python` stage of the aarch64 `base-ubuntu22` variant failed because `test_tcpstore_metadata_exchange` could not create its master `dist.TCPStore` on the CI-assigned fixed port 10507 (5 s connect/validate timeout); it is unrelated to this PR and reproduces on build #3106 as well. Fix the test to let the kernel pick the port (`port=0`) and use a longer TCPStore timeout instead of relying on the pre-allocated `NIXL_TCPSTORE_PORT`.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** Stage 574 "Test Python" (aarch64 / base-ubuntu22 container `nixl-ci-non-gpu-base-ubuntu22-3108-xwgq2-p0c78`) failed: `1 failed, 24 passed, 3 skipped` — `test/python/test_tcpstore_metadata.py::test_tcpstore_metadata_exchange` raised `torch.distributed.DistNetworkError: The client socket has timed out after 5000ms while trying to connect to (127.0.0.1, 10507)`.

**Root cause:** The test constructs a PyTorch `TCPStore` as master on the port CI hands it via `NIXL_TCPSTORE_PORT` and torch's own client validation connect to `127.0.0.1:10507` never completed within the hard-coded 5 s timeout (`[c10d] TCP client failed to connect/validate to host 127.0.0.1:10507 - timed out (try=0, timeout=5000ms)`; the connect timed out rather than being refused, i.e. nothing usable was accepting on that port in the container's netns). The port is not reserved: `.gitlab/test_python.sh:70` calls `get_next_tcp_port` at script start, and that helper (`.ci/scripts/common.sh:38-61`) only does a one-shot `ss -tuln | grep -q :$port` check and then hands the number out — and because the allocation sequence is deterministic (etcd took 10505/10506 from the persisted `/tmp/nixl_tcp_port_0` value 10504), the same port 10507 is picked on every run. The failure is therefore deterministic on this platform, not a one-off: build #3106 (different commit, different aarch64 node, container `...-3106-8th18-c821v`) failed identically at the same line with the same port and the same 5000 ms timeout, while the x86_64 variants of the same builds pass. Nothing in this PR (`iyastreb/improve-makexfer-debug`) touches TCPStore, metadata exchange, or the CI port helper.

**Implicated commit:** `aed5ef2e` — aschwartz12, "test: add Python TCPStore metadata integration (#2148)" (introduced both the test and the `NIXL_TCPSTORE_PORT` wiring in `.gitlab/test_python.sh`)

**File:** `test/python/test_tcpstore_metadata.py:21-28` (port/timeout), with `.gitlab/test_python.sh:70` and `.ci/scripts/common.sh:38-61` (port allocation)

**Suggested fix:** Make the store creation robust instead of depending on a pre-reserved fixed port:
1. In `test_tcpstore_metadata.py`, pass `port=0` so the kernel assigns a free port (the test already reads the real port back via `tcp_store.port` on line 33) and raise `timeout` to ~30 s; if a specific port must be honoured, wrap the `dist.TCPStore(...)` call in a retry loop that picks a new port on `DistNetworkError`.
2. Drop the now-unneeded `NIXL_TCPSTORE_PORT` export at `.gitlab/test_python.sh:70`, or make `get_next_tcp_port` actually hold the port (bind-and-release check immediately before use) rather than checking `ss` minutes earlier.
3. Re-run the aarch64 `base-ubuntu22` variant after the change to confirm; do not treat this as a legitimate failure of the PR — it should not gate merge.

**Related:** PR #2148 (test that introduced this); no existing issue found for the TCPStore timeout — worth opening one tracking the arm64 reproduction (#3106 and #3108).

</details>

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-18

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-build-container-pr` · commit `08ab175b`

**TL;DR:** The container build died in the gRPC step because `git clone https://github.com/grpc/grpc` got an auth prompt from github.com ("could not read Username… No such device or address") — a transient GitHub/network failure unrelated to the PR; add retry/hardening around the source clones in `contrib/Dockerfile` and re-run.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** One of the four parallel "Build image" stages (stage id 233) of `nixl-ci-build-container-pr` #712 failed at Dockerfile STEP 14/53 with `exit status 128` while cloning gRPC.

**Root cause:** Transient failure talking to github.com from inside the build container. The log shows the immediately preceding step (STEP 13, `git clone https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp.git`) succeeded at 10:01:13 and completed its build/install normally, then at 10:02:19 the very next clone failed:
```
Cloning into 'grpc'...
fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address
fatal: expected flush after ref listing
subprocess exited with status 128
Error: building at STEP "RUN git clone --recurse-submodules -b ${GRPC_TAG} ... https://github.com/grpc/grpc ...": exit status 128
```
For a public repo, git only prompts for a username when the server answers 401/403 — i.e. GitHub rate-limited/rejected the anonymous request (or a proxy/DNS blip returned an error page). `No such device or address` is just git failing to open a tty for the prompt. There is no timeout/hang involved (the log is continuous, the failing step lasted ~2 s), and the other three parallel image variants completed their `Build image` stage successfully, so this is environmental flakiness, not a defect from commit 08ab175b (`iyastreb/improve-makexfer-debug` touches transfer debug code, nothing in the container recipe).

**Implicated commit:** none — not a code regression. The clone steps date from the gRPC/Abseil source-build addition in `contrib/Dockerfile`; most recent touches to that file are d2495941 (NirWolfer) and [REDACTED:Hex High Entropy String] (NirWolfer), neither related.

**File:** contrib/Dockerfile:178 (gRPC clone; same exposure at contrib/Dockerfile:161 for Abseil)

**Suggested fix:**
1. Immediate: re-trigger build #712 — the failure is transient and should not reproduce.
2. Durable hardening — give the third-party clones the same retry treatment the DOCA `wget` already has (`--tries=3 --waitretry=5`, line 135). E.g.:
   ```dockerfile
   RUN export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_ASKPASS=/bin/true && \
       for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do \
           git clone --recurse-submodules -b ${GRPC_TAG} --depth 1 --shallow-submodules \
               https://github.com/grpc/grpc && break || \
           { rm -rf grpc; echo "grpc clone attempt $i failed, retrying"; sleep $((i*10)); }; \
       done && \
       cd grpc && ...
   ```
   Setting `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` also makes the real HTTP error visible instead of the misleading "could not read Username" message. Apply the same loop to the Abseil clone.
3. Longer term: these two dependencies are fetched on every image build from the public internet — consider mirroring them internally (as was already done for apt via `APT_MIRROR`, line 85) or vendoring the pinned tags to remove GitHub as a build-time single point of failure.

**Related:** none found — no existing issue/PR in the repo tracks git-clone flakiness in `contrib/Dockerfile`.

</details>
